constraints: Insert rubric execution into _validate as a third stage AFTER command + transcript: call `await run_rubric_graders(task, store, run_id=lifecycle.run_id, attempt_number=attempt.number, transcript=agent_output, worktree=config.worktree, command_passed=command_passed, transcript_passed=transcript_passed, judge_model=config.rubric_judge_model, judge_max_turns=config.rubric_judge_max_turns, now=clock)`. When command_passed or transcript_passed is False the runner short-circuits to [] and no rubric events are emitted -- preserves the existing failure paths byte-identical.

All-rubric-pass (every persisted record has passed=True, which covers both true verdicts and unknown=True): _finalize_attempt with Outcome.SUCCEEDED and _transition(DONE). Matches today's all-pass path.

Rubric-fail (the runner returns a record with passed=False AND payload.unknown is False): inspect the failed rubric's RubricGrader.retry_on_fail via the grader_spec snapshot or by re-reading the matching RubricGrader from task.graders by ordinal. \n   - True (default): _finalize_attempt with Outcome.VALIDATION_FAILED, _transition(FAILED_VALIDATION) with error='rubric grader \'<name>\' failed' (mirrors _grader_failure_error formatting). The next iteration of the outer retry loop will pick up the FAILED_VALIDATION -> READY -> RUNNING cycle.\n   - False: _finalize_attempt with Outcome.VALIDATION_FAILED, _transition(INTERRUPTED) with the same error. No retry consumed (INTERRUPTED is not a retry source).

RubricJudgeError catch in _validate: emit harness.crash with payload {classification: 'rubric_judge_error', grader_name, reason, message}; _finalize_attempt with Outcome.INTERNAL_ERROR; _transition(INTERRUPTED). The existing retry-eligibility check at harness.py:485-515 covers the INTERNAL_ERROR retry behavior.

Emit per-rubric telemetry: harness.rubric_invoked (one per RubricGrader invocation, before the judge call) with payload {grader_name, judge_model, attempt_number}; harness.rubric_verdict (after parse) with payload mirroring the verdict envelope ({grader_name, passed, summary, unknown}); harness.rubric_unknown (only when unknown=true) with payload {grader_name, summary}. To get per-call telemetry, EITHER (a) pass an event-emitter callback into run_rubric_graders OR (b) re-derive the events in the harness from the returned records. Pick one and pin it in tests/test_grader_rubric.py AND tests/test_harness.py so the contract is auditable. If (a) is chosen, update the runner task's exports by adding the callback to the runner signature in this task -- the runner shipped without it, so this is a non-breaking signature extension.

Plumb the worktree path: workflow.py's run_task_file passes `sandbox` into HarnessConfig.worktree when constructing the config. When config.worktree is None and a task has at least one RubricGrader, the rubric runner raises RubricJudgeError per the runner task's defense-in-depth guard. Existing harness tests that build HarnessConfig() without `worktree=` continue to work because their tasks have no RubricGrader -- audit and update any that DO have a RubricGrader to either supply a worktree or remove the rubric grader.

Populate IterationInputs.prior_rubric_findings on retry: in _drive_iterations (or wherever build_iteration_prompt is invoked), before building the prompt, call store.list_grader_results(lifecycle.run_id) ONCE, identify the most-recent attempt that has any rubric records, and select the rubric rows with passed=False AND payload.unknown != True from that attempt. Build the RubricFindings tuple in (attempt_number ascending, then ordinal ascending) order. Pass () when no prior attempts exist or the most-recent attempt had no failing rubric records.

Lifecycle resumed from INTERRUPTED (rubric retry_on_fail=False): when an operator promotes INTERRUPTED -> READY (or the recheck primitive from spec 00004 does), the next attempt's prior_rubric_findings populates from the persisted failing rubric record so the agent sees the critique on resume.
Multiple rubric graders where the first fails: only the first failing record is persisted (cost-order within type). prior_rubric_findings on the next attempt contains the one failing record.
Two rubric graders, both pass: both records are persisted (one per grader); the lifecycle proceeds to DONE.

Rubric grader fails on attempt #1 with retry_on_fail=True, then attempt #2's working agent (now with reviewer feedback in its prompt) emits intent=blocked: the BLOCKED path takes precedence over rubric; rubric is not invoked on attempt #2. prior_rubric_findings from attempt #1 still feeds into the prompt on the attempt where the BLOCKED envelope arrives.
Concurrent attempts on the same lifecycle: optimistic-concurrency on Lifecycle.version (existing semantics) gates the VALIDATING -> * transitions; no new concurrency surface added by this task.
Worktree missing at validation time (rare; spec FR-7 'defense in depth'): RubricJudgeError 'worktree not available' -> INTERNAL_ERROR -> retry-eligible.

An older lifecycle whose grader_results rows do not contain a `summary` key in the rubric payload (data persisted by a different version): treat missing summary as empty string in the prior_rubric_findings construction; the prompt section renders the `(no summary provided)` placeholder.
